Opioid Treatment Program – Initial Intake Assessment

Patient: 34-year-old male presenting for evaluation of ongoing opioid use, self-referred after increasing difficulty controlling use of illicit fentanyl over the past 8 months.

History: Patient reports daily IV use of fentanyl, with escalating tolerance and multiple unsuccessful attempts to cut back on his own. He endorses withdrawal symptoms (myalgias, GI upset, anxiety) when he goes more than 8-10 hours without using. Meets DSM-5 criteria for opioid use disorder, severe, confirmed on structured clinical interview (tolerance, withdrawal, unsuccessful cutting down, craving, continued use despite social/occupational consequences). Patient states he understands methadone maintenance is a long-term commitment and voluntarily elects to enroll in daily dosing rather than pursue detoxification alone; he was counseled on alternatives including buprenorphine office-based treatment and residential rehab but prefers OTP-based methadone maintenance given his prior relapses after short-term detox.

Medical history reviewed: no significant cardiac history, denies chronic pain conditions. Psychiatric history notable for generalized anxiety, untreated. No history of trauma disclosed at this visit. Hepatitis and HIV risk factors discussed given IV use. Not currently pregnant (confirmed by urine hCG, negative).

Physical exam: Vitals stable, afebrile. Track marks noted bilateral antecubital fossae. No acute distress, pupils reactive, mucous membranes intact. Cardiopulmonary exam unremarkable. No signs of active infection at injection sites.

Mental health screening: PHQ-9 score 6 (mild), GAD-7 score 11 (moderate); no acute suicidal ideation.

Labs: CBC and LFTs sent this visit; hepatitis B/C serologies and HIV test drawn; PPD placed for TB screening, to be read in 48-72 hours.

Informed consent obtained and signed, discussing methadone risks (QT prolongation, sedation, respiratory depression), benefits, and alternative treatment options; patient's preference for methadone documented.

Treatment plan: initiate methadone induction per protocol, weekly counseling sessions offered and accepted, referral to on-site psychosocial support group discussed with patient expressing interest.

Withdrawal assessment: COWS score 14 (moderate withdrawal); plan for supervised methadone induction starting at 30mg with close monitoring per protocol.

Safety/overdose: discussed high overdose risk given IV fentanyl use and reduced tolerance risk during induction; naloxone education provided and take-home naloxone kit dispensed today.

Plan: Begin methadone maintenance therapy today per OTP physician order. Follow up in 24 hours for dose reassessment.
